conditions.description: On the last day of each Test Period (commencing with the Test Period ending March 27, 2022), the Total Rent Adjusted Net Leverage Ratio must not exceed the scheduled maximum applicable to that period, increased by 0.50:1.00 during any Covenant Acquisition Increase Period following consummation of a Material Acquisition, subject to the anti-stacking proviso requiring a clean quarter between successive increase periods.

sufficiencyReasons: The base stepped-threshold schedule and the 0.50:1.00 Material Acquisition step-up mechanism are fully represented.

The anti-stacking proviso (requiring at least one clean Fiscal Quarter between successive Covenant Acquisition Increase Periods, potentially delaying a subsequent increase period) is a stateful sequencing rule that cannot be faithfully expressed with the available stateless primitives and is therefore captured as UNSUPPORTED within the gating condition rather than discarded.

Key defined terms ('Total Rent Adjusted Net Leverage Ratio', 'Material Acquisition', 'Test Period', 'Fiscal Quarter') are used but not declared anywhere in the available document package, per Phase 2's own determination; this does not block representing the covenant's operative structure but limits precise computability of the underlying metric and trigger.

provenance.excerpt: On the last day of any Test Period ... the Borrower shall not permit the Total Rent Adjusted Net Leverage Ratio to be greater than (A) ... 5.50:1.00, (B) ... 5.25:1.00, and (C) ... 5.00:1.00; provided that, upon the consummation of a Material Acquisition ... the ratios set forth above ... shall be increased by 0.50:1.00 ...; provided, further, that ... there shall be at least one Fiscal Quarter in which no Covenant Acquisition Increase is in effect between successive Covenant Acquisition Increase Periods ...

irExtensionCandidates.sourceEvidence: §6.10(a): 'provided, further, that notwithstanding the foregoing, there shall be at least one Fiscal Quarter in which no Covenant Acquisition Increase is in effect between successive Covenant Acquisition Increase Periods (which, for the avoidance of doubt, may result in the delay of the commencement of a Covenant Acquisition Increase Period with respect to any Material Acquisition that occurs during another Covenant Acquisition Increase Period or such one Fiscal Quarter period).'
irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: A way to express a recurring 'cooldown/anti-stacking' constraint on a repeatable EVENT_ACTIVE-style temporary override: the override cannot re-activate until at least N periods have elapsed since the prior override period ended, and a new triggering event occurring during an active or cooldown period has its own override period effectively deferred.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: EVENT_ACTIVE models a single trigger->duration override but has no built-in notion of cross-instance history, minimum spacing/cooldown between successive activations, or deferral logic when a new trigger occurs during another instance's active or cooldown window. COMPARE/AND/OR/IF are stateless and cannot reference the sequence of prior activations.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: COOLDOWN_GATED_EVENT (or an activationHistory-aware extension of EVENT_ACTIVE) taking a base EVENT_ACTIVE plus a minimumCooldownPeriod, which computes activation windows accounting for deferral of overlapping trigger events.

Compiled Section 6.10(a) as a single stepped, event-modified ratio maintenance covenant (Total Rent Adjusted Net Leverage Ratio).
The Material Acquisition step-up (+0.50:1.00) is modeled via IF/EVENT_ACTIVE nested inside an ADD against the base SCHEDULE threshold.
The anti-stacking/cooldown proviso is preserved structurally (as an AND operand) but marked UNSUPPORTED rather than silently dropped or force-fit, per the safety-first instruction.

Section 6.10(c)'s equity Cure Right is noted via a dependsOn reference since it materially affects how a breach of this test is ultimately assessed, but was not separately compiled as it falls outside the scope of 6.10(a) itself.

No new tool calls were made beyond the provided context: the listed defined terms (Total Rent Adjusted Net Leverage Ratio, Material Acquisition, Test Period, etc.) were already confirmed by Phase 2 as undeclared anywhere in the document package, so re-querying getDefinition would be redundant.
